source: Wikipedia: Nigel Cross (summary of Cross 1982, 2001, 2006, 2011)
finding: Cross 1982 claimed design has its own culture of knowledge, separate from science and the humanities. The page says this helped found design as an academic discipline.
numbers: No data on that page. Cited: Design Studies 3(4) 221-227 (1982); Cross 2004 Expertise in design 25(5) 427-441; Dorst and Cross 2001 co-evolution 425-437.
quote: things to know, ways of knowing them and ways of finding out about them that are specific to the design area
limits: Encyclopedia summary, not the paper. The 1982 paper itself was paywalled (HTTP 403) and not read. The claim is a conceptual position, not a tested effect.
agent_relevance: The designerly claim is a framing, not a result. Treat it as a hypothesis to test with LLM runs, not as evidence.

source: Wikipedia: Design thinking (criticisms, Lawson 1979, Cross 2023)
finding: The page gives no quantitative evidence that design thinking works. Critics (Kimbell, Vinsel, Iskander) say business design thinking is under-theorised and gives creative confidence without skill. Lawson 1979 found architects use solution-focused strategies and scientists use problem-focused ones. Cross 2023 splits DesignThinking 1 (design-based) from DesignThinking 2 (business-based).
numbers: No effect sizes, no sample sizes. Only pro-effectiveness citation is Liedtka 2018 (HBR), not summarised.
quote: Designers tend to use solution conjectures as the means of developing their understanding of the problem.
limits: Secondary source. Lawson 1979 sample size not given there. Page text was read to 100000 of 106237 characters.
agent_relevance: The strongest what-holds-up point: the designerly claim has weak quantitative backing. Solution-first conjecturing (Lawson, Cross) is the one behaviour with the longest empirical record.

source: Wadinambiarachchi et al. (2024) The Effects of Generative AI on Design Fixation and Divergent Thinking (CHI 2024)
finding: Between-participants sketch study with an example avatar to induce fixation. AI image generation raised fixation on the example more than web image search, and both raised it over no support. AI users made fewer ideas, less variety, lower originality.
numbers: N=60, 20 per condition. 20 minutes sketching. Fixation: GenAI mean .32, 89% CI [.11,.55], Bayes factor 124; image search .27 [.05,.49], BF 42.5. Fluency total effect: image search -.49 [-.9,-.10], GenAI -.29 [-.7,.28], BF 3.2. Originality GenAI -.03 [-.06,.00]. 44% (206/468) of AI images showed humanoid robots like the example. 57% (67/117) of prompts contained robot/chatbot words. NASA-TLX overall F(2,57)=1, p=.37.
limits: Students, one visual task, 20 min, Bayesian models with 89% intervals. Originality effects are tiny. Fluency loss partly from time spent browsing (direct effect after time control was small).
agent_relevance: Replicates the classic fixation result (Jansson and Smith style) with a new inducer. Example text in a prompt can anchor an LLM too. Add a step that names the example features and bans copying them.

source: Chen et al. (2025) Understanding Design Fixation in Generative AI
finding: Proposes GenAI design fixation and tests it with ten novice designers designing chairs with ChatGPT text plus Midjourney images. Most copied ChatGPT prompts into Midjourney unchanged. Human-made chair data had a higher share of unique terms than ChatGPT data.
numbers: N=10 (4 men, 6 women, age 20-26, mean 22.7, SD 3.01). Share of unique terms: ChatGPT 67.4% vs human (Red Dot award data) 78.2%. 30% (n=3) asked ChatGPT directly for initial ideas.
limits: Tiny N, novices only, one product category, comparison data from a different source (Red Dot). Descriptive, no significance tests found in the parts read.
agent_relevance: The fixation cure is in the loop (ask for outliers, rewrite prompts), not in the model. Matches the schema aim to force divergence before convergence.

source: Egea et al. (2024) ChatGPT as an inventor: strengths and weaknesses of current LLMs against humans in engineering design
finding: In a 48-hour prototyping hackathon, ChatGPT-4 directed two human executors. It placed second of six teams. It showed strong concept generation but dropped promising concepts at small difficulties, added needless complexity, and fixated.
numbers: Six teams, over 100 prototypes in the dataset. NERF dart range: team 3 37.66 m (winner), ChatGPT team 14.8 m (2nd), team 2 8.07 m, team 1 6.56 m, team 4 5.06 m, team 5 0.06 m; mean 12.0 m. 97 chat prompts gave 108 codes. 31 of 78 codes on ChatGPT were Instruction and Guidance, 11 Idea Generation, 9 Decision-making.
quote: ChatGPT experiences and is limited by design fixation, both regarding not wanting to abandon a working concept and specific details provided in prompts
limits: One run, one task, one LLM. Humans executed and gave feedback, so it is a hybrid. No repetition, so rank 2 could be chance. The winner beat ChatGPT by over 2.5 times.
agent_relevance: Real evidence of solution fixation in an LLM: it kept optimising one design until told it had hit a plateau, then pivoted late. Fix: a rule to ask for a pivot when gains plateau. It also fixated on the last item of a list in the prompt.

source: Xu, Martelaro, McComb (2026) Supervising Ralph Wiggum: Metacognitive Co-Regulation Agentic AI Loop for Engineering Design
finding: On a battery-pack design task, a plain agent loop (RWL) was beaten by a self-regulation loop (SRL) and by a co-regulation loop (CRDAL) where a second agent monitors metacognition. CRDAL did best and explored the design space further.
numbers: 30 runs per system, Gemini 3.1 Pro, 30 design steps max. Capacity mean Ah: RWL 72.07 (SD 20.52), SRL 106.08 (45.60), CRDAL 141.17 (48.45). ANOVA F(2,86)=21.606, p<0.001, partial eta2=0.334. RWL vs SRL d=0.956; RWL vs CRDAL d=1.846; SRL vs CRDAL d=0.746 (p=0.005). RWL success 29/30. Final designs above 6048 cells: RWL 0, SRL 9, CRDAL 6/30 at mode 8100 cells.
limits: One model, one task. RWL had lowest variance (consistent but stuck). Steps used as cost proxy; the cost table was only partly read.
agent_relevance: Closest to our design: a separate monitor that names fixation and pushes exploration gave d=1.85 over a plain loop. Supports a distinct reflection operator, with the caveat that it is one task.

source: Rosenbaum et al. (2025) Scaffolding Creativity: Divergent and Convergent LLM Personas
finding: Coach-like LLM with divergent and convergent personas, versus a standard answer-giving LLM. Persona users rated the divergent persona higher but idea fluency did not change. Idea originality (embedding distance) was higher across participants. Perception and measured performance diverged.
numbers: 105 recruited, 101 logs: 69 persona, 32 control. 50% design students, 30% engineering. Divergent persona creativity rating 3.65 vs 2.76, g=0.69, p=.003. Convergent persona 2.70 vs 2.76, p=.837. Fluency 8.55 vs 9.23 (ns). Originality (cosine distance to peers) .34 vs .28, p=2.2e-6; all-participant .33 vs .31, p=.02. Within-person diversity .59 vs .59, p=.90. Solution came from me 3.56 vs 4.07, g=-0.52, p=.018.
limits: Unbalanced groups (69 vs 32). Originality measured by an embedding model, only between people. Gains were between-person, not more variety inside one person. Self-report mismatch.
agent_relevance: Alternating divergent and convergent roles (the design-thinking diamond) shifts ideas away from the typical answer. It does not make one run more varied inside itself, so diversity needs many runs or varied seeds.

source: Carichon et al. (2026) IDEAFix: Evaluation Framework for Creative Defixation Prompting in LLMs
finding: Five LLMs were given design briefs with defixation prompts. Every method-inspired prompt (SCAMPER, TRIZ, C-K, Design Thinking, brainstorming, scenario) beat the control on novelty. Simple wild or unconventional prompts did as well as or better than complex method prompts. Output sameness persisted.
numbers: Models: Llama-3.1-70B, Qwen3-30B, Gemini-2.5-Flash, GPT-4o, Grok-4.1-fast; three runs each; 25 prompts. Top-5 novelty gains vs baseline roughly +10% to +41% by method (TRIZ +35.6%, C-K +40.3%, Scenario +30.9%, Design Thinking +18.1% on the rarity panel as read from the figure). Product briefs gave highest novelty and rarity; service briefs lowest. Surprising keywords raised novelty and rarity but cut diversity.
quote: simpler prompts emphasizing such cues tend to outperform more complex, method-based prompts
limits: Percentages were read from a figure with garbled text, so treat them as approximate. Embedding-based novelty, no human raters. No single method won on fluency, novelty, rarity and diversity together.
agent_relevance: Naming the design method in the prompt gives little over a plain be-unconventional instruction. Do not pay tokens for a long design-thinking script; a short divergence cue is enough. Add many samples, because homogenisation stays.

source: Wang et al. (2026) NexusAI: Design Space Exploration through Cognitive Abstraction and Functional Decomposition
finding: A diagram tool that splits LLM ideas into typed What-How-Value fragments and lets users abstract and recombine them. Within-subject study against a text baseline: wider branching, lower workload.
numbers: N=14 within-subject. Average out-degree per node 0.98 vs 0.30, p=0.004. NASA-TLX overall 3.26 vs 4.17, p=0.049. Temporal demand 3.00 vs 4.43, p=0.049. Frustration 2.43 vs 4.36, p=0.006. Performance 5.29 vs 4.14, p=0.004.
limits: N=14, no multiple-comparison correction visible, one baseline. Branching in the log is a proxy for exploration, not for idea quality.
agent_relevance: Decomposing an idea into function, mechanism and value, then re-abstracting, is a testable operator for our agent. Evidence is small but points the same way as the fixation literature.

source: Wang et al. (2025) DesignerlyLoop: Forming Design Intent through Curated Reasoning
finding: Two-layer canvas separating design intent from LLM reasoning. Within-subject test of curated reasoning against a matched baseline: higher usability, controllability, trust, and higher self and expert design quality.
numbers: Formative N=8, main study N=20 designers, 40 design pairs. SUS 77.6 (SD 13.0) vs 69 (SD 19.1), t(19)=2.34. Controllability t(19)=3.65, p=.002; Collaboration t(19)=2.80, p=.012. Self-rated novelty 5.20 vs 4.25 (p=.001). Expert ratings favoured the system on two quality measures (p=.004 and p=.006).
limits: Baseline was the same interface without curation, not a plain chat tool. Designers were experienced with LLM creative tools. Novelty plus usefulness composite is the authors own.
agent_relevance: Making the reasoning chain editable (reject one step, regenerate from there) is a reflection-in-action move. In our scaffold this maps to revisable intermediate states.

source: Diamond of Thought: A Design Thinking-Based Framework for LLMs in Wearable Design (2024)
finding: Design-thinking-structured prompting plus retrieval from a database of 1,603 prototypes and 1,129 products. Ranked IO < CoT < DoT on expert ratings. Not significantly different from human designers.
numbers: Six professional designers (5+ years) rated outputs; Kendall W 0.90-1.00. DoT vs humans p=0.89 (no difference). Some pairwise tests p=0.025, 0.039, 0.017, and diversity vs humans p=0.350. Four design tasks.
limits: Small expert panel, author-built rubric, four tasks. A non-significant gap to humans is not proof of equality. Retrieval is confounded with the design-thinking structure.
agent_relevance: The gain mixes structure and retrieved precedent. We cannot say the design-thinking frame alone helped. A fair test needs retrieval without the frame.

source: MUTATE: Evaluating and Enhancing Divergent Thinking in Interactive LLM Agents (2026)
finding: Interactive benchmark for finding several different solution paths. Frontier LLMs show action fixation under convergence pressure: when one mechanism is blocked they swap tools inside the same mechanism. A method (ReDNA) that separates divergent generation from convergent selection raised path discovery.
numbers: 10 scenarios, 56 path slots. Path discovery: Claude Sonnet 4.6 30/56 (53.6%), GPT-5.4 25/56 (44.6%), Qwen3-235B 22/56 (39.3%), Llama-4-Maverick 13/56 (23.2%), Llama-4-Scout 7/56 (12.5%), human average 44.75/56 (79.9%). GPT-5.4 base 27/56 (48.2%) to ReDNA 38/56 (67.9%), Self-Refine 29/56 (51.8%), EscapeAgent 35/56 (62.5%).
limits: Benchmark by the authors with hand-written scenarios, physical-world puzzles, not design tasks as such. Number of runs per cell not confirmed.
agent_relevance: Splitting generate-wide from select-narrow beat generic self-refine by about 16 points on GPT-5.4. Supports keeping divergence and selection as separate operators.

source: Jansson and Smith (1991) Design fixation (as described in Wadinambiarachchi et al. 2024)
finding: Classic fixation study: designers shown an example with a flaw copied features of it. Cited in the CHI 2024 paper as the model for its own design.
numbers: Four experiments reported in the original, per the secondary description. Exact numbers not read.
limits: Not opened. Second-hand description only.
agent_relevance: Original source for the fixation effect; read before relying on figures.

source: Sio, Kotovsky, Cagan (2015) Fixation or inspiration? A meta-analytic review of the role of examples on design processes
finding: Only the title was seen (in the reference list of the Ralph Wiggum paper). The title frames the open question of whether examples hurt or help.
numbers: None read. Publisher page returned 403.
limits: Not opened. Do not quote effect sizes from this line.
agent_relevance: Key target for a later pass: the moderators of when examples help or hurt.

source: Micheli et al. (2019) Doing Design Thinking: Conceptual Review, Synthesis, and Research Agenda (JPIM)
finding: Cited in the Wikipedia design-thinking article as a 2019 review. Publisher page returned 403. Nothing read.
numbers: None.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Candidate source on whether design thinking has outcome evidence in firms.

source: Cross-paper comparison of the opened sources: effect of AI help on fixation (direction)
finding: Where an example or AI image is shown, fixation goes up (Wadinambiarachchi). Where the LLM is made to alternate divergent and convergent roles, originality across people goes up (Rosenbaum). The two are not contradictory: the first is unstructured exposure, the second structured scaffolding.
numbers: Fixation BF 124 (N=60) vs originality p=2.2e-6 (N=101 logs, unbalanced).
limits: Different tasks, measures and populations. Cannot be pooled.
agent_relevance: Structure of use, not just access, drives the result. Scaffold the use.

source: Cross-paper comparison of the opened sources: method prompts vs plain cues
finding: Method names (TRIZ, C-K, SCAMPER, Design Thinking) do not reliably beat a simple be-wild cue. A design-thinking-framed pipeline with retrieval (Diamond of Thought) reached human parity on four tasks but was confounded with retrieval.
numbers: IDEAFix: all method prompts beat control, simple prompts matched or beat them. DoT: p=0.89 vs humans.
limits: Neither paper isolates the design-thinking frame from other changes.
agent_relevance: Do not assume the designerly frame is the active ingredient. Ablate it.

source: Cross-paper comparison of the opened sources: separate monitor vs same-agent reflection
finding: Two studies point the same way: a separate step that watches for fixation or splits generate from select helps. CRDAL d=1.85 over plain loop; SRL (self-monitor) d=0.96 over plain; co-regulation beat self-regulation d=0.75. ReDNA +19.7 points on GPT-5.4 over base; Self-Refine only +3.6.
numbers: CRDAL N=30 runs per arm; ReDNA 56 path slots per model.
limits: Different tasks (battery pack, physical puzzles). One model family each.
agent_relevance: Separate roles beat single-agent self-reflection in both, matching schema operators for divergence and selection.

source: Failure to find: replications of Cross 1982 as an experiment
finding: No replication or failed replication of designerly ways of knowing as a testable claim turned up in the sources I could open. The claim is conceptual. Testable parts (solution-first conjecture, fixation, co-evolution) have separate literatures.
numbers: Zero replications found. Searches blocked: Semantic Scholar 429, OpenAlex budget exhausted, arXiv API 429, WebSearch budget exhausted.
limits: This is a search failure and a gap, not evidence of absence. Paywalled primary sources (Cross 1982, Dorst and Cross 2001, Lawson 1979, Sio 2015) were not read.
agent_relevance: Next pass should open Dorst and Cross 2001 and Sio 2015 for numbers before the schema leans on them.

source: Gap: no study found that tests LLMs on the designerly claim itself
finding: In the arXiv result lists I read (ten for design thinking plus LLM, twelve for fixation plus LLM), none tests whether an LLM shows solution-first conjecturing or problem-solution co-evolution. Related: IdeaForge 2605.13311 combines TRIZ, Design Thinking and SCAMPER in a multi-agent system and reports more diverse candidates than single-method baselines (abstract only, not opened).
numbers: 10 and 12 results scanned. IdeaForge result is from the abstract only.
limits: Search was by keyword on arXiv only and limited by rate limits.
agent_relevance: An open slot: a controlled test of problem-solution co-evolution for LLM agents.

source: Gap: DesignerlyLoop uses the Cross-style claim as motivation (no test)
finding: The paper states a misalignment: design thinking needs iterative intent formulation, but LLMs treat inputs as complete specifications. It tests an interface fix, not the underlying claim about LLM behaviour.
numbers: N=20 within-subject, as above.
quote: design thinking requires iterative intent formulation, while LLMs treat inputs as complete specifications
limits: The mismatch claim is argued, not measured in the model.
agent_relevance: Matches schema need: treat the first problem statement as revisable.

source: Chen et al. (2025) GenAI design fixation: participant feedback
finding: Participants noticed fixation more in the image model than in the text model, and nearly all copied ChatGPT-made Midjourney prompts with few edits. Few judged the outputs sufficiently innovative.
numbers: Of ten participants, nearly all copied prompts; only two edited them. N=10.
limits: Small interview sample, self-report.
agent_relevance: Users skip the reframe step unless forced. The agent should rewrite its own prompt and check for sameness.

source: Egea et al. (2024) prompt detail anchoring
finding: When the prompt listed the available machines, the LLM fixated on the last item and proposed building everything with it (3D printer or laser cutter). The authors replaced the list with a general description.
numbers: Observed during pilot prompt tests. No counts reported.
limits: Anecdotal pilot observation.
agent_relevance: List order in a prompt can anchor an LLM. Shuffle or summarise option lists in scaffold prompts.

source: Rosenbaum et al. (2025) personality moderators
finding: Individual traits predicted who liked or used the divergent or convergent persona. Agreeableness predicted positive evaluation; extroversion predicted convergent preference; openness related to rating the system above ChatGPT. These links showed only in the persona condition.
numbers: Extroversion with convergent preference r=0.26, p=.035. Agreeableness link r=0.49, p<.001 (to a positive persona evaluation). Control-condition correlations all p>.14.
limits: Correlations on about 66 survey cases, many tests, no correction seen. Self-report.
agent_relevance: Moderator evidence is about humans. For an agent the analogue is task type: when to diverge and when to converge should depend on the task, not be fixed.

source: Carichon et al. (2026) IDEAFix model and brief moderators
finding: Model choice and brief type moderate LLM novelty. Grok and Llama gave more novel, rare and diverse ideas. Product briefs gave the most novel ideas, service briefs the most conventional. Authors link this to training-data familiarity, like human fixation on typical categories.
numbers: Llama-70B median perplexity 70.26 vs mean 1803.32 (outliers). Temperature 0.7 (Qwen, Grok) or 1.0 (others), 3 runs each, 8192 max tokens. Differences reported significant (appendix tables, not read in full).
limits: Appendix tables not opened. Embedding metrics only.
agent_relevance: Task framing changes originality as much as the method prompt. Reframe the task, for example by asking for atypical angles, before sampling.
